title: Two minds about the evening, and a food record that does not add up

rules.label: Righting reflex
rules.text: Advice she did not ask for raises sustain talk; ask permission first.

rules.label: Records under-count
rules.text: Treat a low record as information about recording, not as a lie.

rules.label: Scope
rules.text: Coach habits and food choices; a medical question (her blood pressure) goes to her doctor.

objective: Using motivational interviewing: open questions, affirmations, reflections and summaries

Assessing dietary intake with food records, 24-hour recalls and food frequency questionnaires, and knowing their limits

Eur J Clin Nutr. 2006;60(4):561-565: energy intake under-estimated by about 37% on a 7-day diet record and about 42% on a food frequency questionnaire, against doubly labeled water
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the abstract page. One study of 65 women; used only to show that under-reporting is common and large, not as a number for this client.

brief.situation: You are a nutrition coach. Leila Haddad, 46 (a fictional client), is in her fourth week of coaching. She wants to lose some weight and feel less tired; her weight has not changed in four weeks. Last week she agreed to keep a three-day food record, and she has brought it. You have 45 minutes.
handover: Coaches support habits and food choices within their scope; medical questions go to her doctor.
howItWorks: Each response takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock.
The screen shows what she has said, what you have found, her rapport and stage of change, and the rules that apply now.
When you end the session you write the note and explain your reasoning.

safetyNote: Teaching case for exam practice; fictional client.

openQ.label: Ask an open question: 'How did the week with the food record go?'

effects.log: You ask how the week went.

affirm.label: Affirm the effort: three days written down, even the hard ones

reflect.label: Reflect both sides: 'Evenings are your only downtime, and you also want to feel better in your clothes'
reflect.available: not busy and (isNull(reflectAt) and not isNull(openAt))

effects.log: You reflect both sides of what she said.

ruler.label: Ask how important the change is to her (0-10), then why she did not pick a lower number

effects.log: You ask the importance ruler and the follow-up.

summary.label: Summarize her reasons for change and ask what she makes of them
summary.why: There is not enough of her own talk to summarize yet.

effects.log: You collect her change talk in a summary.

righting.label: Tell her what to do: cut the evening snacks and the wine
righting.why: She has stopped listening to advice.

effects.log: You tell her what she needs to change.
You read the record she brought.

confront.label: Tell her the record cannot be right: she must be eating more than this
confront.available: not busy and (isNull(confrontAt) and not isNull(recordAt))

effects.log: You tell her the numbers do not add up.

explore.label: Ask, without judgment, what is hardest to write down: drinks, weekends, cooking oil, bites while cooking
explore.available: not busy and (isNull(exploreAt) and not isNull(recordAt))

effects.log: You ask what tends to go unrecorded.

recall.label: Do a 24-hour recall of yesterday together, with portion prompts

effects.log: You walk through yesterday meal by meal, with portion prompts.

permission.label: Ask permission, then share that most food records under-count, and ask what she thinks
permission.available: not busy and (isNull(permAt) and not isNull(recordAt))

effects.log: You ask before sharing, then ask her view.

herStep.label: Ask what one small step she would choose for this week

effects.log: You ask what step she would choose.

mineStep.label: Set her goal for her: no food after 8 pm, every day

effects.log: You set the goal for her.

closeSession.label: End the session and write it up
closeSession.why: Finish what you are doing first.

triggers.when: rapport <= 1 and not walkedOut and isNull(closedAt)

effects.log: She gathers her things: 'I don't think this is for me.' She cancels her next sessions.

writeup.question: For the coaching note: where she is in the stages of change and how you could tell, what you did with the food record, and what she decided.

parts.label: Stage and evidence
parts.criteria: Contemplation with ambivalence (wants change, wants her evening), moving toward preparation as her change talk grew; quotes or paraphrases her reasons.
parts.modelAnswer: Contemplation: she wants to feel better and her blood pressure worries her, and her evening is her downtime. With reflections, the ruler and a summary her change talk grew and she picked a step: preparation.

parts.label: The food record
parts.criteria: Reads the low record against a steady weight as under-recording, which is common (diet records under-count substantially), explores what goes unrecorded without blame and checks with a 24-hour recall; does not accuse her.
parts.modelAnswer: 1,250 kcal a day with a steady weight means the record misses things; most records under-count. I asked what is hard to write down and did a recall: evening wine and snacks, cooking oil.

parts.label: Her decision
parts.criteria: A small, specific step she chose (not one imposed), and a check-in.
parts.modelAnswer: Her own step: tea instead of the second glass on weeknights, and logging weekends; a check-in on Friday.

noProgress.when: not isNull(closedAt) and step == "none" and not walkedOut
noProgress.rationale: Ending still ambivalent but with rapport intact keeps the door open; nothing was harmed.

quit.label: She quits coaching
quit.narrative: Told what to do and that her record was wrong, she cancels her sessions and stops recording.

moved.label: Her own step, her own reasons
moved.when: documented == "full" and not walkedOut and step == "hers" and rapport >= 6 and rightingN == 0 and isNull(confrontAt) and not isNull(exploreAt)
moved.narrative: She heard her own reasons, saw what the record missed without being blamed for it, and chose a step she believes in.

partial.label: Some movement, with gaps
partial.narrative: {step == "mine" ? "She leaves with your rule, not hers." : step == "none" ? "She leaves still weighing it, without a step." : rightingN > 0 or not isNull(confrontAt) ? "She chose a step, after some pushing that cost rapport." : isNull(exploreAt) ? "The record's gaps were never explored." : "The note is thin."}

expertPath.text: Open question; affirm the record; reflect both sides of the evening.
Read the record; ask what is hard to write down; a 24-hour recall; ask permission before sharing that records under-count.
Importance ruler and why not lower; summarize her change talk; ask what step she would choose.
A full note: stage, her reasons, the record and recall, her step, the check-in.

moved.headline: Good: her reasons, her step
moved.body: Reflections and the ruler drew out her own reasons; the record became information, not an accusation; she chose the step.

partial.headline: Some movement, with gaps
partial.body: Telling her what to do or that the record is wrong raises sustain talk; a step you choose for her is less likely to last than one she chooses.

quit.headline: Pushed away
quit.body: Advice she did not ask for and an accusation about her record broke the alliance. Ask, reflect and explore first.

time_up.headline: No note
time_up.body: End the session and write the note before the time runs out.

scoring.modelReasoning: Contemplation with ambivalence; OARS and the importance ruler drew change talk; the low record with a steady weight was explored without blame and checked with a recall (records under-count); she chose a small step; a full note.
